**Yes—a separate Lox plugin is worth trying.** I would keep your existing skills while testing it.

I inspected all eight skills and their dependencies against your installed equivalents. These judgments concern the prompts and workflow fit; I have not benchmarked their results.

### Best candidates

- **[PR descriptions](https://github.com/lox/agent-skills/blob/main/writing-pr-descriptions/SKILL.md): likely better.** Stronger checks for stale claims, final scope, and accurate issue-closing language. Its concise Why/What format suits you.
- **[Simplicity review](https://github.com/lox/agent-skills/blob/main/simplicity-review/SKILL.md): my strongest recommendation.** It gives concrete smaller replacements and judges conceptual complexity. Better calibrated than line-count targets or file-size thresholds.
- **[Drafting plans](https://github.com/lox/agent-skills/blob/main/drafting-plans/SKILL.md): better for bounded work.** Much less ceremony. Keep `ce-plan` for larger work needing requirements traceability and integration with `ce-work`.

### Useful alternatives

- **[Writing tests](https://github.com/lox/agent-skills/blob/main/writing-tests/SKILL.md): broadly equivalent principles, shorter guidance.** Your Spade/Termpower test-audit provides stronger regression evidence and should remain.
- **[General review](https://github.com/lox/agent-skills/blob/main/general-code-reviewing/SKILL.md): simpler workflow, less explicit proof.** A good fast-review challenger; your current reviews require stronger reproduction and project-specific checks.
- **[Adversarial review](https://github.com/lox/agent-skills/blob/main/adversarial-code-reviewing/SKILL.md): useful focused alternative.** Strong grounding rules, but no evidence yet that it outperforms your adversarial or multi-model reviews.
- **[Auto review](https://github.com/lox/agent-skills/blob/main/auto-review/SKILL.md): useful new capability.** A bounded review → fix → validate loop. Worth testing locally after the review skills.

### Keep your current babysitter

**[Lox babysitting](https://github.com/lox/agent-skills/blob/main/babysitting-prs/SKILL.md) is a worse fit unchanged.** It can fix and resolve feedback automatically and optionally merge. Your workflow preserves accept/reject decisions and leaves merging to you. Its helper also treats skipped checks as acceptable, so its readiness summary needs judgement.

### Plugin recommendation

Create an independently installable **`lox` plugin**, following your PStack packaging pattern.

Start with the six guidance/review skills plus their documentation companion. Make invocation explicit, preserve upstream prompts, and record small local adaptations. Add auto-review later.

Compare both sets on the same frozen PR, plan, and diff, using the same model and fresh sessions.

Before publishing a redistributed plugin, clarify licensing: this snapshot has a simplicity-review license, but no repository-wide license.

The [full comparison and packaging proposal](/Users/staggart/.codex/worktrees/0afa/agent-kit/.ai/research/2026-10-01-lox-skills-comparison.md) contains the details. Nothing was installed or changed in your existing plugins.
